data.rationale: Reachability: the packet fuzzer (src/fuzzers/packet-fuzzer.cc) feeds chunks as DLT_RAW packets into packet_mgr->ProcessPacket; an IPv4/IPv6 packet with protocol ICMP whose type is ICMP_UNREACH or ICMP_TIMXCEED routes to ICMPAnalyzer::NextICMP4 -> Context4 (ICMP.cc:598), which calls ExtractICMP4Context(caplen, data) (line 617). ExtractICMP4Context (line 324) only requires len >= ip_hdr_len + 4 before calling GetContextProtocol (line 366-367); the same insufficient check exists in ExtractICMP6Context (line 426). GetContextProtocol then computes transport_hdr = ip_hdr start + ip_hdr_len (lines 257-259) and dereferences a full transport header: a struct icmp (lines 286-295), struct tcphdr (lines 302-304), or struct udphdr (lines 310-312) of 8-20 bytes, without any check that that many bytes remain within the packet buffer. Only 4 bytes past the embedded IP header are guaranteed, so reading the sport/dport/type/code fields reads up to ~16 bytes past the end of the heap-allocated packet buffer (the fuzzer chunk from FuzzBuffer::Next is an exactly-sized heap allocation), producing an ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ. The root cause is the missing remaining-length check in GetContextProtocol before parsing the embedded transport header.
